items.prompt: int live=0; try { Guard g(live); throw runtime_error("x"); } catch(const runtime_error&) { /* inspect live */ } With the displayed nonthrowing Guard destructor, what is live inside the handler?

options.text: 1, because local destruction waits until the handler returns.
options.why: A local object in the exited try scope is destroyed during unwinding before control enters this handler.

options.text: 0, because Guard is destroyed before this handler is entered.
options.why: The fully constructed Guard decrements live during normal exception unwinding. If that destructor threw a second exception during unwinding, terminate would be called instead of normal recovery.

options.text: 0 only if the catch explicitly calls g.~Guard().
options.why: g is out of scope in the handler, and automatic destruction has already occurred; explicit destruction here would be invalid and unnecessary.

options.text: An unspecified integer because all locals are discarded without destruction after throw.
options.why: C++ unwinding destroys fully constructed automatic objects whose scopes are exited; this is the RAII behavior being tested.
